clusters.title: A 'no (bolt) holes in the web / flanges / short leg / elsewhere' is read as 'the whole member is welded', or a lazy skip runs across the negation and counts web lines + The bolt words are there but no bolt size or hole count is read (glued '3/4inbolts', '2perflange', 'bolted 3/4in'): the asks are non-blocking, so only yielding is computed
clusters.root_cause:
[tension-hole-negation-scope] reader.js tensionCommon line 1612 `if (/no\s+bolt\s+holes/i.test(t)) welded = true;` fires on any 'no bolt holes', with no check of what follows ('in the web', 'in the flanges', 'elsewhere', 'the short leg has ...') and even after a bolt size and hole counts were read. findHoles line ~1205-1206 (the weldedWord regex) has the same unscoped `no\s+bolt\s+holes|...|no\s+holes\b`. The welded test at line 1610 also ignores H.cutFlange, H.lines and H.across, so 'no holes in the web' plus '4 holes in the flanges' becomes welded (tcap-08). Welded mode skips every hole count, so only yielding is computed (702 printed where 596.2 is right). findHoles line 1147 (web lines) and its 'through ... lines of' twins use the lazy skip `(?:\S+\s+){0,5}?`, which crosses ', no ' and reads the negated 'bolts/holes through the web' as web lines (tcap-09/10/11). H.web then wins over H.noWeb. pipeline.js line 3347-3352 (the 'mentions bolts or holes' guard) is switched off by its own exclusion `\bno\s+(?:bolt\s+)?holes?\b`. I checked this on the branch: the same text without 'no bolt holes in the web' prints 596.2.
[tension-holes-unread-nonblocking] reader.js tensionCommon line 1625 (B.ask 'bolt_dia') and lines 1649/1673 (B.ask 'holes_count') are raised with no kind, so they default to kind 'value'. pipeline.js markReaderStops (2997-3015) blocks only 'stop' and 'need', so the engine runs with empty hole boxes as 'no holes' (702 / 318.6 printed). The safety guard in pipeline.js 3346-3352 covers only tension_capacity/tension_net_area, not tension_select (tsel-10, 12). It tests `\b(?:bolt(?:s|ed)?|holes?)\b`, and there is no word boundary inside the glued 'inbolts' / '2holes' / '3bolts' (tcap-19, tsel-11). The trigger is pipeline.js normalizeTyped line 1864: the glued-unit splitter refuses 'in' followed by a letter ('3/4inbolts'). findHoles line 1117 needs \s+ before 'per' and a \b(holes?|bolts?)\b in the text ('bolted' does not count).
clusters.fix_plan:
[tension-hole-negation-scope] reader.js only, plus one small pipeline hunk. (1) findHoles weldedWord regex (~1205): `no\s+bolt\s+holes` and `no\s+holes\b` count as welded only when NOT scoped. Add a negative lookahead for `\s+(?:are\s+|is\s+)?(?:in|through|on|at)\s+(?:the\s+|its\s+|either\s+|each\s+|any\s+)?(?:web|stem|flanges?|(?:short|long|outstanding|other)?\s*legs?)` and `\s+elsewhere`. Check 'X has no bolt holes' with a slice test on the text before the match (ES5, no lookbehind). (2) tensionCommon line 1612: use the same scoped test, and add `&& !F.bolt && !H.perFlange && !H.cutFlange && !H.web && !H.lines && !H.perLine && !H.across && !H.inSection && !H.forBolt`. Line 1610: add the same count slots. (3) noWeb/noFlange regexes: make the article optional ('no bolt holes in web'), so the scoped phrase still sets web_holes = 0. (4) Line 1147 and its twins: the token skip may not cross a comma, a semicolon or a negation: `(?:(?!(?:no|not|none|without)\b)[^\s,;]+\s+){0,5}?`. If H.web and H.noWeb are both set, raise a count_web ask (kind 'need'), never a silent override. (5) pipeline.js 3349: the exclusion keeps only an unscoped 'no holes'. ANSWER where the reading is single: tcap-01/02/03/05/07 give 596.2 / 471.1 / 152.3, tcap-06 gives 168.2 (Case 8), tcap-08/09 give 596.2, tcap-04 gives U = 0.90. ASK: tcap-10 then falls to the '2 lines in the flanges' halving rule (cluster tension-geometry-multiplier: 1 or 2 per flange), and tcap-11 (no flange word) asks holes_count. MUST NOT CHANGE: a bare 'no bolt holes' / 'there are no holes' / 'welded' / 'all connections are welded' stays welded and yielding only. Also unchanged: '(there are no bolts in the web)' with flange counts (noWeb), her May 2024 Q8 'four lines ... through its flanges' (2 per flange), and gross-section-yielding mode.
[tension-holes-unread-nonblocking] (1) reader.js tensionCommon 1625, 1649/1650, 1673: when the member is not welded and the text contains bolt|hole|rivet as a SUBSTRING (not \b, so glued words count), raise these asks with kind 'need'. The gate then asks ONE question instead of printing yielding only. (2) pipeline.js 3347: extend the guard regex to tension_select and use the substring test (one-line hunk). (3) Coverage only, after (1)-(2) are in: normalizeTyped 1864 also splits `(\d)(in)(?=bolts?|holes?|dia)`, and `(\d)(per|holes?|bolts?|lines?)\b` becomes 'N per'. These are splits only and change no reading. ANSWER where the reader then reads the size and counts. ASK (need) otherwise. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'select lightest w8 welded' (no bolt word, no ask), 'no holes' / welded members, plates and angles whose counts are read, selections where the hole counts are read.

clusters.title: A tension count's multiplier or a size's kind is chosen silently: two angles, both legs, bolts per flange vs holes, each side of the web, halved lines, hole diameter vs bolt diameter
clusters.root_cause: [tension-geometry-multiplier] reader.js findHoles / tensionCommon / findBolt take one reading of a geometry word without a second check. (a) tensionCommon lines 1585 and 1602: angles = 2 only for a 2L name or the adjacent `(double|pair of|two) angles`. 'two L4x4x1/2 angles' (the shape name in between) drops the count (tcap-12/13: half the strength). (b) Nothing reads 'both legs' / 'each leg'. findHoles yields H.lines = 1, so line ~1661 sets holes_across = 1, and the connection rule at ~1713 (`memberIsAngle && (H.locLeg || F.bolt ...)`) gives Case 8 'one leg' (tcap-14/15/16). (c) findHoles line ~1091 `(WN) ... (holes?|bolts?) (in|across|through) (each|every|both) flanges?` takes a BOLT count per flange as holes across, even when 'N bolts per line' is in the text (6 bolts/3 per line = 2 lines; tcap-17). (d) The each-side-of-the-web doubling (~1070-1075) runs only when no per-flange count was read, and cgApply had already set perFlange = 1 from the same phrase (tcap-18). (e) tensionCommon 1641-1644 halves cutFlange 'N lines of bolts in/through the flanges' to N/2 per flange (confidence medium) without an ask. That is right for her Q8 'four lines', but '2 lines ... in the flanges' has two readings (tsel-13). (f) findBolt line 1228 (pattern 4) returns kind 'bolt' even when its noun is 'holes' ('holes are 15/16 in. in diameter'), so the existing bolt_or_hole path never runs and hole + 1/8 is applied to a hole (tcap-22/23).
clusters.fix_plan: [tension-geometry-multiplier] reader.js only. (a) Lines 1585/1602: also accept `\b(?:two|2|double|pair\s+of)\s+(?:L\s?\d[\w\/.\s-]{0,14}?\s+)?angles?\b` when exactly one L name is in the text: ANSWER (angles = 2). (b) For an angle with 'through/in both legs' or 'each leg': U = 1.0 (Case 1, every element connected, her case). Set holes_across = 2 x lines only when a per-leg line count is read ('one line in each leg'); otherwise ASK holes_across (kind 'need'). Never Case 8. tcap-14 gives 140.2, tcap-15 gives U = 1.0, tcap-16 gives An = 2.875. (c) Line ~1091: if the noun is 'bolts' and a per-line count exists, holes per flange = N / perLine when it divides evenly (ANSWER 2 for 6/3). Otherwise ASK count_perFlange ('need'). A bolt count is never holes. (d) Each-side doubling: also apply it when the per-flange count came from the same 'on each side of the web' clause (ANSWER 2 per flange). If another per-flange number was typed, use the existing conflict ask. (e) Line 1641: keep the halving for N >= 4 (her Q8). N = 2 'lines in/through the flanges' raises a count_perFlange question naming both readings. The existing count_ mechanism (pipeline markReaderStops) empties the box and asks. (f) findBolt line 1228: kind = /hole/i.test(noun) ? 'hole' : 'bolt'. The existing bolt_or_hole / MISSING path then asks. Never add 1/8 to a hole. MUST NOT CHANGE: 2L names, 'double angles', HW 3-23 'one each side of the web' (2 per flange), 'N holes per flange', one-leg angles (Case 8, U from her table), 'four lines ... through its flanges' = 2 per flange.

clusters.title: The Euler form takes K = 1 by default, ignores bracing and axis words, and ignores a typed E
clusters.root_cause: [euler-form-gaps] reader.js FILL.column_euler (1969-1996). Line 1991 raises B.ask('euler_K', ..., choices) for any end other than pinned-pinned, and that becomes kind 'choice'. pipeline.js mergeBoxes (549) gives the empty, non-required K box its engine default of 1, and markReaderStops (2997) ignores 'choice', so a flagpole or a fixed-fixed column is worked out with K = 1 (185.12 printed; ccap-267/296). Lines 1984-1986 read ONE length (Ls.lx || Ls.common). Ls.brace and the axis words ('about the x axis') are never used, and the frozen engine takes r = min(rx, ry) (ccap-286/218). The engine's Euler form has no E box. The typed 'E = 30000 ksi' is listed as unused, but pipeline.js unusedQuestions (2754) marks a stress non-blocking, so the gate lets it through (ccap-285).
clusters.fix_plan: [euler-form-gaps] reader.js column_euler, plus at most one pipeline condition. (1) Line 1991: raise euler_K with kind 'need' (keep the choices in the text). Euler with a non-pinned end has two K sets (theoretical vs her design K), so ASK and never use the default 1. (2) Raise a 'stop' with one sentence and no number ('this Euler form uses one length and the smaller r; NOT answered here') when Ls.brace.fraction or Ls.brace.above is set, when Lx and Ly differ, or when the words name an axis (about the x|strong|major axis). The frozen engine cannot apply rx or two lengths. (3) A typed 'E = N' with N not equal to 29000 raises a 'stop' (no E box). Equivalently, unusedQuestions marks an unplaced 'E =' stress as blocking. MUST NOT CHANGE: pinned-pinned Euler from a shape name, 'A = 11.9 in^2, r = 3.67 in' given in the question, a printed K (line 1989), 'ry = ...' as the only r, the 'Euler applies?' 113.4 check.
